subject: Critical Thinking
title: Ibn al-Haytham: The First True Scientist
description: A quick, practical guide to Ibn al-Haytham: The First True Scientist.

hook.text: Before Galileo, before Bacon, an 11th-century Arab polymath invented the scientific method. His name: Ibn al-Haytham.

buildup.text: Working in Cairo, he wrote 'Kitab al-Manazir': the first work to insist that scientific claims must be verified by.

discovery.text: His method: question assumptions, design controlled experiments, measure results, & trust evidence over authority.

twist.text: He openly challenged ancient authorities, insisting that truth comes from reason and experimentation, not old texts.

climax.text: Ibn al-Haytham's experimental method predated European science by centuries.

punchline.text: Trust evidence, not authority. He said it a thousand years ago.

quiz.question: What was Ibn al-Haytham's revolutionary contribution to thinking?
options: Insisting that scientific claims must be verified by controlled experiments, not authority

details.summary: Ibn al-Haytham, working in 11th-century Cairo, pioneered the experimental scientific method centuries before Europe's Scientific Revolution. His Book of Optics used controlled experiments, mathematical proof, and systematic doubt to overturn ancient Greek theories of vision.
details.whyItMatters: Ibn al-Haytham demonstrated that authority must yield to evidence, establishing the principle that experimentation, not reputation, decides truth.
takeaways: He insisted on testing claims through controlled experiments
His work on optics corrected errors by Ptolemy and Euclid
He anticipated the modern scientific method by centuries

faq.question: How did Ibn al-Haytham's approach differ from the Greek tradition?
faq.answer: Greeks relied primarily on logical deduction from first principles. Ibn al-Haytham demanded that hypotheses be tested through physical experiments and mathematical analysis. He systematized doubt as a method of inquiry.

faq.question: What was Ibn al-Haytham's most important discovery in optics?
faq.answer: He proved that vision occurs when light enters the eye from external objects, overturning the ancient emission theory that eyes send out rays. He demonstrated this through experiments with the camera obscura.
